Comic 8 Revolution: Santet K4bin3t is a 2025 Indonesian horror action comedy film directed by Fajar Bustomi and written by Adhitya Mulya. The film is both a sequel and the fourth installment of the Comic 8 franchise, following Comic 8 (2014) and Comic 8: Casino Kings Part 1 & 2 (2015–2016). Produced by Falcon Pictures, it was released nationwide in Indonesian cinemas on 24 December 2025.
The film features a combination of comedy, action, horror, and political satire, introducing a new generation of stand-up comedians from the "Mencari Komplotan Baru Comic 8: Revolution" auditions as the lead characters, supported by several senior comedians and actors.
Synopsis
The story centers on Ki Bagus and Ni Gendis, a pair of powerful shamans harboring a grudge against the government. Utilizing high-level black magic, the two plot a santet (black magic) attack against the president and the cabinet members as part of an effort to shake the country's stability.
The plan begins to unfold when a high-ranking state official falls victim to the curse, triggering panic within the palace circles. The government subsequently tasks the Republic Intelligence Agency (BIR) to investigate and neutralize the threat. The operation is led by Pakde Indro, assisted by an agent named Oki.
To approach the target, BIR recruits eight new agents with diverse backgrounds and personalities. These agents infiltrate the residence of Ki Bagus and Ni Gendis by posing as domestic workers. During their undercover mission, they must face various mystical rituals, supernatural disturbances, and unexpected situations that lead to conflict and chaos.
Cast
Supporting cast and cameos
Production
This film marks a change of directors within the Comic 8 universe, with Fajar Bustomi replacing Anggy Umbara, who helmed the previous installments. The production also serves as a platform for cast regeneration by featuring eleven new stand-up comedians selected through an open audition held by the production house.
The members of the new squad underwent a period of quarantine, acting workshops, and physical training for several months before filming began. Principal photography lasted for over a month and took place across various locations, including several island regions.
Release
The film's official trailer was released on 22 November 2025 across Falcon Pictures' digital platforms and received widespread attention on social media. The film was released simultaneously in Indonesian cinemas on 24 December 2025.
